summary.text: Cliff Johnson is the Democratic nominee for Mississippi's 1st District. A civil rights lawyer and former federal prosecutor, he directs the MacArthur Justice Center at the University of Mississippi School of Law and teaches there. He describes his campaign as focused on working people, democracy and independence from party.

paragraphs.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from Mississippi College (1989) and a J.D. from Columbia Law School (1992).
After a federal clerkship, worked three years as an associate at the Jackson law firm Butler Snow, then five years as an Assistant U.S. Attorney.
Was a partner for 13 years at the Jackson firm Pigott & Johnson, then joined the Mississippi Center for Justice.
Was a Fulbright Scholar at the Raoul Wallenberg Institute in Lund, Sweden, in 2005-2006.

Directs the MacArthur Justice Center at the University of Mississippi School of Law, where it has litigated cases on cash bail, debtors' prisons and appointed counsel for indigent defendants, and supervises students in its clinic.
Was named a Public Justice National Trial Lawyer of the Year in 2016 and Mississippi Trial Lawyer of the Year for 2017-18 by the Mississippi Association for Justice.
Describes himself as a lawyer who has practiced in Mississippi for 33 years and as a lifelong Democrat.
Won the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary with 63.4% of the vote over Kelvin Buck.
